edits.new:
Completion of earlier adverse episodes does not imply completion of the life they partly constitute. Those episodes cannot now be relieved, but the next development can still improve how that continuing life goes. This identifies an alterable continuation; it does not establish a priority for altering it. Causal inactivity of the past is therefore insufficient to settle the ethical question.

The stronger affirmative premise would be that **alleviating an independently warranted serious shortfall in the good realized through a continuing life can give an available improvement additional significance**. That requires identifying the shortfall, defending its ethical relevance and explaining how this response addresses it. Mere continuity or a larger past pain count does not establish those claims. Where defended, the ground might concern a different whole-life benefit or greater moral importance of a benefit; neither interpretation permits counting the same relief twice. It supplies no general rule of decreasing lifetime weights.

The strongest rival need not deny any of those past experiences, their badness, or the moral significance of either present relief.

edits.new:
**Anders Herlitz, “Health, priority to the worse off, and time,” Medicine, Health Care and Philosophy 21, 517–527 (2018), [publisher full text](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11019-018-9825-2).** The source contributor read all five main sections and note 1; root rechecked the abstract, opening discussion, and selected theoretical-justification and combination passages. Neither inspected the cited works or empirical evidence; the paper's numerical examples are not used here. Accessed 6 October 2026; link-only, with no imported original bytes.

**Bounded synopsis:** Herlitz defends considering both lifetime and prospective disadvantage. Equal lifetime health totals can coexist with unequal status, dependence and opportunities during particular periods. His second argument distinguishes health quantities from whole-life welfare, which may depend on temporal development and social relations. A richer lifetime appraisal can therefore support prospective priority. He retains lifetime fairness while leaving the combination unsettled. These arguments do not derive greater priority from ended adversity alone under our matched-effects controls, or derive moral weight from generated continuity. Our use is a boundary for the stronger proposal, not its proof or adoption of a health-unit scale.

**Our use:** distinguish history-sensitive patient benefit, moral priority and adequacy of a representation.

### Supporting scope and the continuing object of improvement

The follow-up review distinguishes completion of adverse episodes from completion of the life they partly constitute. This identifies what a current response can still improve; it does not derive extra priority from continuity. The stronger shortfall-sensitive ground remains an explicit ethical proposal to defend. Both interpretation as additional whole-life benefit and interpretation as greater moral importance must avoid double-counting the same relief. The new Herlitz reading constrains this proposal without establishing it; McKerlie's full paper remains unread.

Historical-priority adjudication is a supporting extension, not a required prior step for the contributory minimum. The controlled rivals already grant each relief-ground and dispute relative strength. The governing connection remains generative unfolding, differentiated realization and impairment, their joint ethical quality, and responsive transformation. C1/C2 remain local interfaces. This corrects the research-order ambiguity in the preceding “next” language without declaring either those interfaces or the whole foundation complete.

A separate read-only audit confirms the existing [formal interpretation limit](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/noninstrumental-concern/README.md): operational `Eligible` contains no justified-selection-criterion field; `select` copies evidence into authorization and does not determine an award winner. A permitted beneficial outcome therefore cannot automatically be interpreted as an authorized relief-based verdict. This confirms the prior distinction between selection and implementation rather than discovering a new counterexample. No code change, added exclusion axiom or Lean rerun follows.

The argument and scope contributors supplied separate read-only reviews. The [follow-up edit record](HISTORY-PRIORITY-SCOPE-EDITS.json) and [checks](HISTORY-PRIORITY-SCOPE-CHECKS.json) preserve this round's narrower claims and file scope.
